title: Scoped service-account delegation and short-lived proxy credentials
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a scoped delegation model for service accounts that enables issuance of short-lived proxy credentials (TTL tokens) with least-privilege scopes. This ticket covers API/CLI UX, audit-tag propagation, owner approval controls, integration with RBAC v2 role mapping, and SSO/SAML identity binding for delegated flows.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create delegation policies that grant a subset of service-account permissions for a bounded TTL (1m-24h)
Proxy credentials include audit tags that surface in the audit log and console trace for end-to-end attribution
Delegated tokens honor RBAC v2 constraints and SSO group mappings; cannot escalate beyond owner's privileges
UI and API endpoints for creating and revoking delegations are documented and covered by e2e tests
Policy linter warns on broad allow rules and suggests least-privilege alternatives
implementation_notes: Introduce /v2/service_accounts/:id/delegations endpoint (POST/DELETE/GET). POST request accepts 'scopes', 'ttl_seconds', 'purpose', and 'approver_required' flags.
Generate cryptographically signed short-lived tokens with embedded delegation claim (delegation_id) and audit_tag header for downstream services to persist.
Enforce server-side validation against RBAC v2: expand requested scopes -> check subset of owner's effective permissions (including SSO group-derived roles). Reject if request is superset.
Add a synchronous owner-approval webhook flow for delegations > 1h or with admin-level scopes. Provide explicit fallback for emergency 'break-glass' with audit and email escalation.
Extend audit log schema with fields: delegation_id, principal_owner, requested_scopes, approver, ttl_seconds, reason.
Console: new Delegations tab on service-account detail page listing active delegations with revoke button and audit links.
Add server-side rate limits for delegation creation (per-service-account) and a short cooldown to mitigate token sprawl.
Policy linter: implement heuristics to convert wildcard or broad resource patterns to least-privilege alternatives and include code suggestions in API response (HTTP 422 with suggestions).
Backwards compatibility: Legacy service-account API still valid; delegations are opt-in and recorded as sub-resources. No change to existing tokens issued before rollout.

open_questions: Should we allow cross-org service-account delegation for partner integrations? (security recommended: no by default)
What metrics should be surfaced in the console for delegated-token usage (tokens issued, max concurrent active delegations, avg TTL)?
Do we need a managed key rotation policy for delegation signing keys separate from main service-account keys?
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Token sprawl and privileged tokens remaining active longer than intended. Mitigation: strict TTL caps, revoke API, and lifecycle job to sweep stale delegations.
Risk: Delegations could be used to bypass RBAC if validation logic is incomplete. Mitigation: multi-layer checks (API layer + policy engine) and sign-off from security team before rollout.
Risk: Audit logs might not propagate to downstream storage. Mitigation: add end-to-end tests and required audit_tag header enforcement in runtime.
Risk: User confusion in console about who created vs. who approved delegation. Mitigation: show both creator and approver with timestamps and link to approval activity.
